prompt: Put the order of work in an incident as the lesson gives it.
Why did Bia roll back D047 instead of letting Rafa fix the faulty change?

choices.text: Because Rafa was not sure the retry was the cause
choices.why: Even certainty would not have changed the call; undoing stops harm sooner.

choices.text: Undoing stops the harm sooner than diagnosis
choices.why: Right. Every minute diagnosing was another minute of double charges.

choices.text: Because rollbacks fix the bug permanently
choices.why: The bug was fixed the next day; the rollback only removed it.

choices.text: Because the policy forbids fixes during incidents
choices.why: No such rule; it was a judgement about speed.

prompt: Match each mitigation to the situation it fits.

pairs.right: the harm started with a deployment
the change was released behind a flag
the harm is in one place you can route around

prompt: The rollback at 18:15 stopped new duplicate charges. Why did the incident continue until 21:10?

choices.text: Because the rollback failed and was retried
choices.why: It worked; no duplicate came after 18:15.

choices.text: Because the team was writing the postmortem
choices.why: The postmortem was booked for Friday.

choices.text: Because the faulty change was still running
choices.why: It was rolled back at 18:15.

choices.text: Charges already made had to be refunded
choices.why: Right. Restored is when harm stops; resolved is when its consequences are repaired.

prompt: What makes a mitigation cheap to choose in the middle of an incident?

choices.text: It was prepared in advance
choices.why: Right. A one-command rollback, flags around risky changes, a runbook.

choices.text: A senior engineer decides it
choices.why: Seniority does not make it fast; preparation does.

choices.text: It is chosen after the diagnosis
choices.why: Then it is as slow as the diagnosis.

choices.text: It is approved by leadership
choices.why: Approval adds time; the IC decides.

prompt: The rollback started at 18:04 and finished at 18:15. How many minutes did it take?
Which line is written the way the lesson asks a scribe to write?

choices.text: 18:02 the retry logic is broken
choices.why: A guess written as if it were known.

choices.text: around six, we decided to roll back
choices.why: No exact time, and no name on the decision.

choices.text: 18:02 Bia decides to roll back D047
choices.why: Right. A time, a decision and who made it.

choices.text: rollback went fine
choices.why: No time, and an interpretation rather than an event.

prompt: Which rules save a postmortem? Choose every one that applies.

choices.text: Every time in one zone, written the same way
choices.why: Right. Mixed zones swap events.

choices.text: Write each line at the time, not later
choices.why: Right. Late lines have wrong times.

choices.text: Record what was tried and did not work
choices.why: Right. The first thing everybody forgets.

choices.text: Write only the decisions, not the observations
choices.why: Observations are half of what the postmortem needs.

prompt: Why is scribe a good first role for somebody new to incidents?

choices.text: Because it needs no attention
choices.why: It needs a great deal.

choices.text: They see the whole response
choices.why: Right. And contribute something nobody else has time to do.

choices.text: Because scribes cannot be blamed
choices.why: Nobody is blamed in a good postmortem.

choices.text: Because it can be skipped if they are busy
choices.why: Skipping it is the mistake the lesson warns about.

prompt: "18:02 Rafa suspects BIL-218, the retry change" is better than "18:02 the retry change is the cause". Why?

choices.text: It stays true even if the guess is wrong
choices.why: Right. It records a fact about what somebody thought.

choices.text: Because names must appear in every line
choices.why: Names help on decisions; the point here is fact against guess.

choices.text: Because ids are easier to search
choices.why: Searchable, and not the reason.

choices.text: Because the second one is too short
choices.why: Length is not the problem.

prompt: The first duplicate charge was at 17:21 and service was restored at 18:15. How many minutes were the shops harmed?
Of those 54 minutes, 17 passed before anybody noticed. What share is that, to the nearest whole percent?
Which phase of the 30 September incident could only have been shortened by better detection?

choices.text: The rollback
choices.why: That is mitigation, and it was already quick.

choices.text: The refunds
choices.why: Cleanup happens after detection.

choices.text: The decision to roll back
choices.why: That was mitigation-first's opportunity.

choices.text: The 17 minutes before anybody noticed
choices.why: Right. No speed in the response recovers them; lesson 18.

prompt: Why does the lesson warn against averaging incidents into a single MTTR?

choices.text: Because MTTR is not a DORA metric
choices.why: Time to restore is one; the problem is the averaging.

choices.text: Because incidents cannot be timed
choices.why: The lesson just timed one.

choices.text: One long incident dominates and the shape disappears
choices.why: Right. Like lesson 2's average cycle time.

choices.text: Because leadership prefers medians
choices.why: Preference is not the argument.

prompt: Why does timeline.py tag each event with a kind such as detect or restore?

choices.text: To make the timeline look tidier
choices.why: Tidiness is a side effect.

choices.text: To find what matters, fast
choices.why: Right. By a program, or by a tired person.

choices.text: Because the chat tool requires it
choices.why: No tool requires it; it is a convention.

choices.text: To hide the names of the people involved
choices.why: Names stay in the text.

prompt: DORA's time to restore stops when harm stops; the shops also lived through the time to ___, when every refund was done.
Put the steps of handing over incident command in order.
items: the outgoing IC writes a summary in the channel
the incoming IC reads it and asks questions
the incoming IC says out loud that they have command

prompt: An incident is restored but refunds are still running. What does the lesson allow?

choices.text: Downgrading it, but not closing it
choices.why: Right. Closing would tell support there is nothing left to say.

choices.text: Closing it at once
choices.why: Not before it is resolved.

choices.text: Keeping it at SEV1 until the postmortem
choices.why: Nobody is being harmed; the severity can come down.

choices.text: Handing it to another team
choices.why: Nothing suggests another team should own it.

prompt: What does the IC do before closing a resolved incident? Choose every one that applies.

choices.text: Post a final update to every audience
choices.why: Right. In users' terms.

choices.text: Make sure the evidence is kept
choices.why: Right. Before retention deletes it.

choices.text: Book the postmortem
choices.why: Right. Within a few working days.

choices.text: Name the person who caused it
choices.why: Postmortems are blameless, lesson 15.

prompt: Why should the outgoing incident commander actually leave after handing over?

choices.text: Because the rota requires eight hours of rest
choices.why: Rest matters; the reason here is command.

choices.text: Because the new IC might blame them
choices.why: Blame is not part of it.

choices.text: Because the channel has too many people
choices.why: Crowding is a separate problem.

choices.text: Staying to help splits command again
choices.why: Right. One person decides at a time.

prompt: D047 carried four changes and was undone in eleven minutes. Which earlier lesson's argument does that support?

choices.text: Lesson 9's: count items instead of estimating
choices.why: Unrelated to rollback time.

choices.text: Lesson 12's: leave slack in the plan
choices.why: Slack helps respond; batch size makes undoing cheap.

choices.text: Lessons 5 and 7's: small batches are cheap to undo
choices.why: Right. Before August, eight-change releases took over two hours.

choices.text: Lesson 3's: walk the board right to left
choices.why: That is about items, not releases.

prompt: The incident was resolved at 21:10, starting from the first duplicate charge at 17:21. How many minutes is that?
